rationale: A wins because it keeps its hands on the facts: "Allbirds adds a wholesale partner as it pulls back from its own stores" is a clean channel tension and admits the partner name is missing. B has good bones, but "DTC brands are shrinking to survive" turns one company's cuts into a sector trend before the proof exists, and "finally make its shoes last" sneaks in a durability indictment the update did not give it. That is how a useful angle becomes a story a reporter can kill in one email.
gaps_in_A: "as the turnaround plan starts to bite" implies the margin improvement is caused by the turnaround before the causal breakdown exists.
"The prevailing belief in DTC retail is that growth comes from expanding the range and the store footprint" is plausible beat context, but it is not in the supplied facts and needs support.
"durability is the chronic knock against natural-material shoes" smuggles in category history the update did not provide; keep it as a question unless sourced.
gaps_in_B: "DTC brands are shrinking to survive" overclaims a sector trend from one Allbirds update. One company cutting SKUs is not a trend piece without comparables.
"brands are choosing fewer, better bets over growth-at-all-costs" is analysis masquerading as fact; the update only says Allbirds cut its range by 40% and closed stores.
"swaps wool for a sugarcane blend" is inaccurate. The update says a sugarcane-and-wool blend, not a swap away from wool.
"finally make its shoes last" goes past the fact pattern. Allbirds says the blend is more durable than the original wool runner; that is not proof the old shoes failed to last.
